extraction.rai:dataCollection: This is a survey/review paper that describes and analyzes existing VQA datasets (DAQUAR, COCO-QA, COCO-VQA, FM-IQA, Visual7W, Visual Genome, SHAPES) rather than collecting a new dataset. The reviewed datasets were assembled through various methods including: NLP-based automatic generation of QA pairs from image captions (COCO-QA), Amazon Mechanical Turk crowdsourcing for human-generated questions and answers (COCO-VQA, Visual Genome, Visual7W), manual annotation by human annotators (DAQUAR, FM-IQA), and synthetic scene generation (SYNTH-VQA). Source images came from existing repositories including NYU-DepthV2, COCO, and YFCC100M/Flickr100M.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis; Manual Human Curator; Web API; User-generated content data
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The authors note they were unable to retrieve the English version of the FM-IQA dataset from the provided download link.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images from NYU-DepthV2 Dataset (DAQUAR), Microsoft COCO dataset (COCO-QA, COCO-VQA, FM-IQA, Visual7W), YFCC100M/Flickr100M (Visual Genome, Visual7W), and synthetic cartoon scenes (SYNTH-VQA). COCO-QA QA pairs were derived algorithmically from COCO image captions. COCO-VQA questions and answers were collected via Amazon Mechanical Turk workers.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT) workers were employed to generate questions for COCO-VQA images by being asked to 'Stump a smart robot,' and a separate pool of workers were hired to generate answers. Each question was answered by 10 independent annotators. For DAQUAR-consensus, an average of five human annotated ground truth answers per question were collected. For Visual Genome, annotators used free-form and region-specific question prompting methods. For Visual7W, annotators provided plausible answers by answering questions without seeing the image.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: For COCO-VQA, the consensus-based evaluation metric uses AccuracyVQA = min(n/3, 1), where n is the number of annotators agreeing with the algorithm's answer; full score awarded if 3 or more annotators agree. For DAQUAR-consensus, average consensus (weighted toward more popular answers) and min consensus (agreement with at least one annotator) were used. Inter-human agreement on COCO-VQA is approximately 83.3%.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: NLP algorithm used to derive QA pairs from COCO image captions for COCO-QA dataset
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Language biases in datasets allow image-blind models to achieve high accuracy using questions alone; yes/no questions in COCO-VQA are biased toward 'yes' answers (~59% of the time); questions about object presence and scene attributes have strong language priors; DAQUAR contains exclusively indoor scenes limiting question variety; COCO-QA questions are limited to four types derived from COCO captions; attentive mechanisms may attend to biased regions rather than task-relevant regions due to dataset biases
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: DAQUAR is too small to train and evaluate complex models and contains only indoor scenes with clutter and extreme lighting; COCO-QA has grammatical errors and nonsensical questions due to flawed NLP generation, and only four question types; COCO-VQA contains subjective opinion-seeking questions without single objective answers, inter-human agreement is only 83.3%, and over 13% of yes/no questions have both 'yes' and 'no' repeated by more than three annotators; FM-IQA requires human judges making iterative development impractical; Visual Genome's answer diversity makes open-ended evaluation significantly more challenging; multiple-choice evaluation allows systems to exploit answer biases rather than reasoning about images; existing datasets do not provide detailed breakdown of question types making it difficult to evaluate performance on specific question types; current datasets are insufficient to evaluate whether an algorithm has 'solved' VQA
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: VQA could aid blind and visually impaired individuals by enabling them to query images on the web and in the real world; VQA could improve human-computer interaction as a natural way to query visual content; VQA can be used for image retrieval without metadata or tags
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training and evaluating VQA algorithms; serving as a component of a Visual Turing Test for image understanding; aiding blind and visually impaired individuals in getting information about images; improving human-computer interaction for querying visual content; image retrieval without metadata or tags
